intervals.label: candidate host of JUNO-TAO (conceptual design report)
intervals.locator: TAO CDR (arXiv:2005.08745), abstract page; "A ton-level liquid scintillator detector will be placed at about 30 m from a core of the Taishan Nuclear Power Plant."
intervals.note: Start is the submission month of the TAO conceptual design report, which names the plant as the host; interval of the neutrino-physics use only.

intervals.label: hosting JUNO-TAO (assembly)
intervals.locator: IAEA TM talk (April 2025), slide "Assembling in Taishan"
intervals.note: Interval of the neutrino-physics use only: assembly of the TAO detector in the plant began in September 2024. The plant itself (two EPR units in operation, two more possibly to follow) is not dated here; status `construction` is the status of the TAO installation, which is why this facility record is marked `construction` rather than `active`.
intervals.quote: Assembling in Taishan • Started from Sept. 2024

name: Taishan Nuclear Power Plant
notes: Plant description from the TAO CDR: "Taishan Nuclear Power Plant locates in Chixi town of Taishan city in Guangdong province, 53 km from the JUNO experiment. It has two cores currently in operation."

summary.plain: A nuclear power plant on the coast of Guangdong, China, with two of the world's most powerful reactors; a small detector, TAO, is being installed in a basement about 44 metres from one core to measure its antineutrinos precisely for the nearby JUNO experiment.
summary.technical: Taishan Nuclear Power Plant, Chixi town, Taishan city, Guangdong, 53 km from JUNO: two EPR cores of 4.6 GW thermal power each in operation (two more possibly later); host of the JUNO-TAO near detector.
